instructions.instruction_content: Peel and chop eggplant and pumpkin into medium-sized pieces.
Heat butter and add onions and garlic in a medium sized pot set to medium to high heat. Sauté for 2 minutes until softened but not browned.
Add pumpkin and eggplant. Sauté for an additional two to three minutes.
Add water just to cover the vegetables. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to a simmer and cook until the vegetables are soft.
Add the chopped callaloo, stir and cook for an additional 3 minutes.
Pour the vegetable mixture into a colander and let drain.
After vegetable mixture has been drained return it to the pot and mash vigorously with a potato masher or a thick whisk.
Add salt and pepper. Adjust seasoning to taste.

Peel the potatoes and cut them into evenly sized chunks. Reserve a few apple slices for step 3, then peel and chop the remaining apples. Boil the potatoes in salted water for about 10 minutes, then add the chopped apples and cinnamon stick. Boil for another 10 minutes or until both the apples and potatoes are tender.
In the mean time bake the streaky bacon in a dry frying pan until crispy and set aside to drain on paper towels.
Melt 1 tsp of butter in a frying pan. Add the reserved apple slices, maple syrup and a sprinkling of ground cinnamon. Let simmer until the apple slices are soft.
Prepare a plate with one whisked egg and one plate with sesame seeds. Cut your cheese into the required size. The smaller it is, the easier it is too handle.
Dip the cheese into the egg and make sure it coats all sides. Then dip the cheese into the sesame seeds and make sure it is covered everywhere.

Heat a non stick frying pan on high until nice and hot. Put the cheese slice in and bake until the sesame seeds are brown. You have to do this rather quickly or the cheese will melt completely. Turn and bake the other side.
Drain the apples and potatoes and mash them together. Taste and add cinnamon and salt where needed. Remove the cinnamon stick before mashing
Divide the apple and potato mash between plates. Top with the crispy bacon and caramelized apple slices, and serve with the warm sesame-crusted cheese.
Cook the meat: Place the flank steak in a pot with 1 L of beef stock and a little salt. Cook over low heat for about 2 hours, until tender and easy to shred.
Shred the meat: Once cooked, drain and shred the meat using two forks.

Prepare the vegetables: Sauté the chopped onion, red pepper and garlic in 1 tbsp of extra virgin olive oil. Add cumin, oregano, paprika and salt to taste. Stir in the shredded beef and cook for a few minutes until the flavors are well combined.
Make the dough: In a bowl, combine 2 1/2 cups of warm water with a pinch of salt. Gradually add 2 cups of precooked white cornmeal while mixing until a soft dough forms. Let it rest for 5 minutes.
Form the arepas: Divide the dough into 6 portions, shape into balls, and flatten into thick discs.

Cook the arepas on a griddle or skillet over medium heat for about 5–7 minutes on each side until golden. If needed, finish in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 10–15 minutes until cooked through.
Fill: Slice the arepas open on one side, fill with the hot shredded beef, and top with grated cheese.

measurements.measure_value: 2 cups, plus 1 tbsp for egg wash

instructions.instruction_content: Rinse the dried sorrel under cold water. Place it in a medium saucepan with 2 cups of water and the orange zest.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 15–20 minutes until the sorrel is tender. Add a little extra water if needed.
Split the vanilla pod lengthwise and scrape out the seeds. Add the vanilla seeds, brown sugar, ground ginger and ground cinnamon to the saucepan. Stir until the sugar dissolves.

Simmer uncovered over low heat for 15–25 minutes, stirring regularly, until the mixture reaches a thick, spreadable jam consistency. Remove from the heat and allow to cool. Finely chop or blend the softened sorrel if a smoother texture is desired.
Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Lightly dust a clean work surface with the all purpose flour. Roll out the thawed puff pastry until it is large enough to completely enclose the brie wheel.
Place the brie wheel in the centre of the puff pastry. Spread 2–3 tablespoons of the cooled sorrel jam over the top of the cheese.
Fold the pastry around the brie, trimming any excess dough and pressing the edges together to seal completely. Place the wrapped brie seam-side down on the prepared baking sheet.
Mix the beaten egg with 1 tablespoon of water. Brush the top and sides of the pastry with the egg wash. If desired, decorate with the leftover pastry and brush the decorations with egg wash.
Bake for 20–30 minutes until the puff pastry is golden brown, crisp and fully cooked, and the cheese inside has softened.
Remove from the oven and allow the baked brie to rest for 5–10 minutes before cutting. Serve warm with the remaining sorrel jam on the side if desired.
Transfer any leftover sorrel jam to a clean, covered container and refrigerate within 2 hours. Use within 5 days. Refrigerate leftover baked brie within 2 hours and consume within 3 days.
Cut 1.5 kg of beef (preferably chuck or stewing beef) into large pieces. Pat dry with paper towels and season lightly with salt and turmeric.
Heat 3 tablespoons of oil in a large pot. Add the sliced onions and sauté until light golden.
3. Add garlic, green chilies, and tomato; cook until softened.
Add 2 tsp ground coriander, 2 tsp ground cumin, 1 tsp black pepper, 1 tsp ground cinnamon, 1/2 tsp cardamom, 1/2 tsp cloves and 1/2 tsp bay leaf.
5. Add beef pieces and stir on medium heat until the meat is well coated with spices.
Pour in 5 cups of beef stock and enough water to almost cover the beef. Cover and simmer gently for 1.5–2 hours, or until the beef is tender. Add more water during cooking if needed.
7. Remove beef carefully and set aside. Strain and measure the broth.

Rinse and soak the basmati rice for 20–30 minutes, then drain. Measure the rice and the reserved broth. Add enough water to the broth to reach approximately 1.5 cups of liquid per cup of rice, or follow the rice package directions. Add the rice, adjust seasoning and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low, cover tightly and cook for approximately 15–20 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.
10. Place the beef pieces over the rice and steam on low heat for 10 minutes so flavors combine.
12. Fluff rice and serve beef mandi with salad or chutney.
Crack the two eggs into a bowl, add a pinch of salt and whisk until well combined.
Heat a non-stick frying pan over medium heat and melt 1 tsp of butter.
Pour the beaten eggs into the pan and place the two slices of bread side by side on top. Immediately flip each bread slice so both sides are lightly coated with egg.
Cook until the underside of the omelette is set, then carefully flip the entire omelette. Fold the overlapping edges of the omelette inward over the bread.
Fold one slice of bread over the other to form a sandwich. Cook until both sides are golden brown and the eggs are fully set. Serve warm.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add the breadfruit and cook for approximately 30 minutes, until tender but still firm enough to slice.
Remove the breadfruit from the pot and allow it to cool until safe to handle.
Using a sharp knife, cut the breadfruit into thin rounds. Remove the skin and core from each slice.
Gently fold each slice into a taco shell shape and secure it with two wooden toothpicks.
Heat the frying oil in a deep, heavy-bottomed pot to approximately 175°C (350°F). Make sure the breadfruit slices are dry before frying.
Using tongs, carefully lower the shaped breadfruit into the oil. Fry in small batches until golden and crisp. Do not adjust the toothpicks while frying.
Remove the shells with tongs and drain on paper towels. Allow them to cool slightly before removing all toothpicks. The shells are now ready for your preferred filling.
Before you do anything, freeze your bacon slices that way when you're ready to prep, it'll be so much easier to chop!
Wash the potatoes and cut medium dice into square pieces. To prevent any browning, place the already cut potatoes in a bowl filled with water.
Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Tilt the skillet so the oil spreads evenly.
Drain the potatoes and pat them dry with paper towels. Add them to the skillet and season with salt, pepper and 1/8 tsp of allspice.
Cook for 10–15 minutes, stirring the potatoes regularly, until golden brown and nearly tender. Reduce the heat if they brown too quickly.
Chop the bacon and add it to the potatoes. Cook for another 5–8 minutes, stirring regularly, until the bacon is crispy and fully cooked and the potatoes are tender.
Reduce the heat to medium-low, add 1 minced garlic clove and toss. Add the parsley and adjust the seasoning to taste.
Let the garlic cook until fragrant, about one minute.
Just before serving, drizzle over the maple syrup and toss. Let that cook another minute, giving the potatoes a caramelized effect.

Heat the remaining tablespoon of olive oil in a separate non-stick frying pan over medium-low heat. Crack in the two eggs and cook until the whites are fully set and the yolks reach your preferred doneness.
Divide the breakfast potatoes and crispy bacon between two warm bowls. Top each bowl with a fried egg and garnish with parsley. Serve immediately.
Pat the chicken wings dry with paper towels. Do not wash the raw chicken.
Separate the drumettes and flats at the joints, if necessary. Remove and discard the wing tips.

Using kitchen shears, carefully cut around the meat and tendons at the narrow end of each drumette. Push the meat toward the wider end of the bone to form a lollipop shape. For the flats, carefully remove the smaller bone and push the meat toward one end of the remaining bone.
Season the chicken with 1 tsp black pepper, 1 tbsp paprika, 1 tbsp minced garlic and 1 tsp salt. Toss until evenly coated and let rest in the refrigerator for 15 minutes.
Coat the seasoned chicken evenly with 4 tablespoons of cornstarch, shaking off any excess.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep, heavy-bottomed pot to 175°C (350°F). Use enough oil to submerge the chicken without filling the pot more than halfway.

Carefully lower the chicken into the hot oil using tongs. Fry in small batches for approximately 8–12 minutes, depending on size, until golden and crispy and the internal temperature reaches 74°C (165°F). Measure the temperature in the thickest part without touching the bone.
Remove the chicken lollipops using tongs and drain on a wire rack or paper towels. Allow to cool slightly before serving warm.

Prepare the ingredients: thinly slice the pork and mushrooms, cube the tofu, and slice the spring onions. If using dried wood ear mushrooms, rehydrate them according to the package instructions, drain and slice.
Bring 2 1/2 cups of chicken stock to a boil in a saucepan. Add the thinly sliced pork and simmer for 5–7 minutes, or until fully cooked.
Add the salt, sugar, sesame seed oil, pepper, hot sauce, 2 tablespoons of vinegar and soy sauce. Stir to combine.
Add the tofu, mushrooms and wood ear mushrooms. Simmer gently for 5–7 minutes, or until the mushrooms are tender and fully cooked.

In a small bowl, whisk together 1 tablespoon of cornstarch and 2 tablespoons of cold water. Slowly pour the mixture into the simmering soup while stirring. Cook for 1–2 minutes until slightly thickened.
Lightly beat the egg in a small bowl. Slowly drizzle it into the simmering soup while gently stirring to create thin egg ribbons. Continue simmering until the egg is fully cooked.
Taste the soup and adjust the seasoning if necessary. Divide into bowls, garnish with sliced spring onions and serve hot.
Place the 250g of cubed bread in a large bowl. Pour over the 250ml of milk, add a pinch of salt and let soak for 10–15 minutes.
Peel and finely grate the potatoes. Squeeze out any excess moisture. Add the potatoes, grated cheese, eggs and chopped parsley to the soaked bread mixture.
Finely chop the onion. Melt 1 tablespoon of butter in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 4–5 minutes until softened and golden. Add it to the bread mixture.
Add the 100g of flour and gently mix until combined. Shape the mixture into round dumplings and flatten them into patties approximately 1.5 cm thick.

Heat the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter in a frying pan over medium-low heat. Fry the dumplings in batches for approximately 5–7 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure the potatoes are tender and the egg mixture is fully set.
Meanwhile, heat 1 litre of vegetable stock in a separate saucepan until gently simmering.
Divide the cheese dumplings between four bowls, pour the hot vegetable stock around them and serve immediately.
Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Wash and dry the two large potatoes and pierce them several times with a fork.
Place the potatoes directly on the oven rack or on a baking tray. Bake for 60–90 minutes, depending on their size, until the flesh is completely tender when pierced with a knife.
While the potatoes are baking, grate the 150g of cheese. Finely chop the onion and red pepper.
Combine the chopped onion and red pepper in a bowl. Season with salt, pepper and a pinch of red chilli flakes. Mix well and set aside.
Remove the baked potatoes from the oven. Carefully slice each potato lengthwise without cutting all the way through. Gently open the potatoes while keeping the skins intact.
Add 1 tablespoon of butter and half of the grated cheese to each potato. Using a fork, mash the hot potato flesh inside the skin until the butter and cheese have melted and the filling is creamy.
Divide the seasoned onion and red pepper mixture between the two potatoes. Serve immediately while the potatoes are hot and the cheese is melted.

recipes.name: Lakror me Kungull Summer Squash Pie

instructions.instruction_content: Preheat the oven to 180°C (356°F). Wash and grate the two summer squash.

In a large mixing bowl, combine the grated squash, 3 tablespoons of sugar, 2 eggs and 1/4 teaspoon of bicarbonate of soda. Gradually add the 300g of flour and mix until a thick, sticky mixture forms. If the mixture is too runny, add a little more flour.
Lightly grease the base and sides of a large round baking tray approximately 5 cm deep with olive oil.
Transfer the mixture to the baking tray and spread it evenly. Lightly coat your hands with olive oil and gently smooth the surface until flat and slightly glossy.
Bake for approximately 40 minutes, until the top is golden brown and the centre is fully set. Insert a toothpick into the centre to check that no wet batter remains.
Remove the pie from the oven and allow it to cool before slicing into squares and serving.
Crumble the 500g of day-old bread into small pieces. Gradually sprinkle with up to 100ml of cold water until lightly moistened but not soggy. Cover with a damp cloth and leave for 30 minutes.
Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large, deep frying pan over medium heat. Lightly crush the 4 garlic cloves and fry for 3–5 minutes until golden and fragrant. Remove the garlic and set aside.

Add the 200g of diced pork to the same pan. Fry for approximately 6–10 minutes, depending on the size of the pieces, until browned and cooked through. For whole-cut pork, ensure an internal temperature of at least 63°C (145°F), followed by a 3-minute rest. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining 2 tablespoons of olive oil to the same pan. Add the moistened bread and cook over medium heat, stirring frequently for approximately 15 minutes.
Remove the garlic skins and return the garlic and cooked pork to the pan. Add 1/4 teaspoon of black pepper and stir to combine.
Continue cooking over medium-low heat for another 10–15 minutes, stirring frequently, until the bread crumbs are golden, slightly crispy on the outside and soft inside.
Divide the Migas between four plates and serve immediately while warm.
Peel the potatoes and carrots and cut them into small, uniform cubes.
Place the potatoes and carrots in a large pot and cover with water. Add 1 teaspoon of salt and 1/2 tablespoon of white wine vinegar.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium and simmer for approximately 15 minutes, until the potatoes and carrots are tender but still hold their shape. Drain and allow to cool.

If using raw sausages, cook them according to the package instructions until fully cooked, reaching an internal temperature of 71°C (160°F) for pork or beef sausages, or 74°C (165°F) for poultry sausages. Allow to cool and cut into small cubes. If using ready-to-eat cooked sausages, simply dice them.
Place the 4 eggs in a saucepan and cover with water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 10–12 minutes until hard-boiled. Transfer to cold water, peel and cut into small cubes.
Dice the 3 dill pickles, finely chop the 4 spring onions and 2 tablespoons of fresh dill, and drain the canned peas.
In a large bowl, combine the cooled potatoes, carrots, sausages, hard-boiled eggs, pickles, peas and spring onions.
Add 1 cup of mayonnaise and the chopped dill. Gently mix until all ingredients are evenly coated. Season with 1/4 teaspoon of pepper and adjust the salt to taste.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving chilled. Ensure the cooked ingredients are refrigerated within 2 hours of cooking.

Preheat the oven grill (broiler). Halve the red pepper lengthways and remove the seeds and stalk. Line a grill pan with foil and arrange the pepper halves skin-side up alongside the unpeeled garlic cloves, red chilli and tomato.
Grill for 2 minutes, turn the tomato and grill for another 2 minutes. Remove the tomato and allow it to cool slightly before peeling, removing the seeds and roughly chopping it.

Continue grilling the pepper, chilli and garlic for 4–5 minutes, or until the pepper and chilli skins are charred and the garlic has softened. Turn and remove individual ingredients as needed to prevent burning.
Once cool enough to handle, peel the pepper, chilli and garlic. Remove the chilli seeds and roughly chop the pepper and chilli.
Spread the hazelnuts and almonds on the grill pan and toast for 2–3 minutes, watching closely to prevent burning. Allow to cool slightly.
Wash the parsley and finely chop it together with the toasted hazelnuts and almonds in a food processor. Transfer the mixture to a small bowl and set aside.
Heat 3 tablespoons (45ml) of olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the roasted pepper, garlic and chilli and cook for 3 minutes, stirring regularly.
Tear the bread into small pieces and add it to the frying pan. Cook for 2–3 minutes, turning the pieces until lightly golden.

Transfer the cooked pepper mixture and bread to a food processor. Add the chopped tomato, 2 tablespoons of red wine vinegar, the remaining 75ml of olive oil and salt to taste. Pulse until a coarse sauce forms. Allow to cool, then stir in the chopped nuts and parsley.

Ensure the tiger prawns are fully cooked, peeled and deveined. Arrange the chilled prawns on a serving plate alongside a bowl of Romesco sauce and serve with cocktail sticks. If preparing the sauce ahead, refrigerate in a covered container within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Keep the prawns refrigerated until serving and follow their package storage instructions.
Bring a small saucepan of water to a boil. Gently lower the egg into the water and cook for 10–12 minutes until hard-boiled.
Transfer the egg to a bowl of cold water for 3–5 minutes to stop the cooking. Peel the egg, slice it in half and set aside.
Bring a separate saucepan of water to a boil. Cook the noodles according to the package instructions until tender, then drain.
Heat 2 cups of vegetable stock in a saucepan over medium heat until gently simmering.
Add 1 tablespoon of soy sauce, 1/2 teaspoon of chilli sauce and 1/8 teaspoon of pepper to the vegetable stock. Stir and simmer for 2–3 minutes. Taste and add salt only if needed.
Place the cooked noodles in a serving bowl and pour the hot seasoned broth over them.
Top the noodles with the two egg halves and 1 tablespoon of sliced spring onions. Serve immediately while hot.

measurements.measure_value: As needed for soaking and cooking

instructions.instruction_content: Place the 200g of dried kidney beans in a large bowl, cover generously with cold water and soak for 8–12 hours or overnight. Drain and discard the soaking water, then rinse the beans.

Place the soaked kidney beans in a large saucepan and cover generously with fresh water. Bring to a vigorous boil for at least 30 minutes, then reduce the heat and simmer until the beans are completely tender, approximately another 30–60 minutes.
Drain the cooked kidney beans, reserving some of the cooking liquid. Rinse the 1 1/2 cups of rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear. Dice the onion.

Return the cooked beans to the saucepan. Add the rice, diced onion, 400ml of coconut milk, 1/2 teaspoon of black pepper and 1 teaspoon of salt. Add enough reserved bean cooking liquid to bring the total cooking liquid to approximately 2 1/4 cups, including the coconut milk.
Place the whole Scotch bonnet pepper on top of the rice mixture without cutting or piercing it. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat to low and cover with a lid.
Simmer for 15–20 minutes, or until the rice is tender and the liquid has been absorbed. If the rice is still firm, add a small amount of hot water and continue cooking.
Remove the saucepan from the heat and carefully remove the whole Scotch bonnet pepper. Let the rice rest, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff gently with a fork and serve warm.

recipes.name: Sichuan Style Stir-Fried Chinese Long Beans

instructions.instruction_content: Wash the Chinese long beans thoroughly, trim the ends and cut them into pieces approximately 5cm long. Pat them completely dry. Either green or purple Chinese long beans can be used.
Lightly crush the Sichuan peppercorns and cut the dried chillies into small pieces. Remove some of the chilli seeds if you prefer a milder dish.
Heat 1 tablespoon of peanut oil in a wok or large, deep frying pan over medium-high heat.
Add the Chinese long beans and stir-fry for 6–10 minutes, tossing regularly, until the beans are lightly blistered and tender but still slightly crisp.
Reduce the heat to medium-low. Add the dried chillies and crushed Sichuan peppercorns. Stir-fry for 30–60 seconds until fragrant, taking care not to burn the spices.
Add 1/4 teaspoon of salt, 1/2 teaspoon of sugar and 1 teaspoon of soy sauce. Toss everything together and cook for another minute until the beans are evenly seasoned.
Remove the pan from the heat and drizzle with 1 teaspoon of sesame seed oil. Toss well and serve warm as a side dish.

Use only commercially prepared, ready-to-eat salted herring fillets. Do not use raw herring. If the package recommends soaking to remove excess salt, soak the fillets in cold water in the refrigerator according to the package instructions.
Drain the herring thoroughly, pat dry with paper towels and cut into bite-sized pieces.
Peel and thinly slice the onion. Place the herring in a clean container with the olive oil, allspice berries, whole black peppercorns and bay leaf.
Cover and refrigerate at 4°C or below for 1 hour to allow the flavors to develop. Do not leave the fish marinating at room temperature.

Remove the whole spices and bay leaf. Serve chilled with the sliced onion, lemon wedges and chopped dill. Refrigerate leftovers promptly and consume within 24 hours or sooner if required by the package instructions.

Rinse the pickled grape leaves under cold water and soak them in fresh water for 10–15 minutes to remove excess salt. Drain carefully and remove any tough stems. Set aside any torn leaves for lining the saucepan.
Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear. Chop the onion and dill, and squeeze the lemon.
Heat 3 tablespoons of olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Add the ground allspice, cinnamon and pine nuts. Stir for 1–2 minutes until fragrant, then add the rinsed rice, raisins and tomato sauce.
Add 1 cup of chicken stock and season lightly with salt and pepper. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook over low heat for 8–10 minutes until most of the liquid is absorbed but the rice is still firm.
Remove the saucepan from the heat. Stir in the chopped dill and half of the lemon juice. Allow the filling to cool until comfortable to handle.

Lay a grape leaf flat with the veined side facing upwards and the stem end facing you. Place approximately 1 tablespoon of rice filling near the stem end. Fold the bottom and sides over the filling, then roll gently. Avoid rolling too tightly, as the rice will expand during cooking. Repeat with the remaining leaves and filling.
Line the bottom of a saucepan with the reserved grape leaves. Arrange the stuffed grape leaves snugly inside, seam-side down, in even layers.

Pour the remaining cup of chicken stock, remaining tablespoon of olive oil and remaining lemon juice over the rolls. Add enough water to nearly cover them if necessary. Place a small heatproof plate on top to prevent them from unrolling. Cover and simmer gently over low heat for 35–45 minutes, or until the rice and grape leaves are tender. Add a little hot water if the saucepan becomes dry before the rice is cooked.

Remove the saucepan from the heat and allow the stuffed grape leaves to rest for 10 minutes. Carefully remove the plate and transfer the rolls to a serving dish. Serve warm or chilled. If serving chilled, refrigerate within 2 hours of cooking.
Finely dice the onion and red pepper, and mince the garlic. Measure out the ground cumin, paprika, salt and black pepper.
Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the onion and red pepper and sauté for 4–5 minutes until softened.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the ground beef and cook for 6–8 minutes, breaking it apart with a wooden spoon, until browned and fully cooked to an internal temperature of 71°C (160°F).

Add the tomato puree, ground cumin, paprika, salt and black pepper. Stir well and cook for another 2–3 minutes until the filling is flavorful and any excess moisture has evaporated. Cover and set aside.
Peel the green plantains, pat them dry and cut them into approximately 1 1/2-inch thick slices.
Heat the remaining vegetable oil in a deep, heavy-bottomed saucepan to 160°C (320°F). Ensure the saucepan is no more than half full of oil.
Carefully lower the plantain slices into the hot oil using tongs. Fry in small batches for 5–7 minutes until softened and lightly golden.
Remove the plantain slices with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Allow them to cool for approximately 3–5 minutes until safe to handle but still warm.
Using a clean citrus squeezer or plantain cup press, gently press each plantain slice into a cup shape. Be careful not to press so hard that the bottom breaks.
Increase the oil temperature to 175°C (350°F). Carefully fry the plantain cups in small batches for another 2–3 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Remove and drain on paper towels.
Reheat the ground beef filling if necessary. Spoon the warm filling into each crispy plantain cup, dividing it evenly between the cups.
Arrange the stuffed plantain cups on a serving plate and serve immediately while warm and crispy.

measurements.measure_value: For cooking rice and sealing rolls

instructions.instruction_content: Rinse the 300ml of sushi rice in cold water several times until the water runs mostly clear. Drain well.
Cook the sushi rice according to the package instructions. Once cooked, leave it covered for 10 minutes.
Combine 60ml of rice vinegar, 2 tablespoons of caster sugar and 1/2 teaspoon of salt in a small saucepan. Warm gently while stirring until the sugar and salt dissolve. Do not boil.

Transfer the cooked rice to a wide bowl. Gently fold the vinegar mixture into the rice without crushing the grains. Spread the rice out and allow it to cool to room temperature before assembling the rolls.
Drain the canned tuna thoroughly and mix it with 3 tablespoons of mayonnaise in a bowl. Cut the cucumber into thin strips.

Place a nori sheet shiny-side down on a bamboo sushi mat. Dampen your hands with water and spread approximately one-quarter of the rice evenly over the nori, leaving a 2cm strip uncovered along the far edge.
Arrange one-quarter of the tuna mixture and cucumber strips in a horizontal line across the rice, slightly below the centre.
Lift the near edge of the bamboo mat and gently roll the nori over the filling. Continue rolling while applying light, even pressure. Dampen the uncovered edge with water to seal the roll.
Repeat with the remaining nori sheets, rice, tuna mixture and cucumber. Using a sharp, damp knife, cut each roll into 6–8 evenly sized pieces.
Arrange the sushi rolls on a serving plate and serve with soy sauce for dipping. Serve promptly and refrigerate any leftovers within 2 hours of cooking the rice.
Warm 1 cup of milk until lukewarm, approximately 35–38°C. Stir in the instant yeast.
Add 1/4 cup of granulated sugar, the cardamom, vanilla extract, salt and approximately two-thirds of the flour. Mix until combined.
Gradually incorporate the remaining flour until a soft dough forms. Add the 5 tablespoons of softened butter and knead for approximately 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Divide the dough into six equal portions and shape each into a round bun. Place them in a greased muffin or cake tin. Cover and allow to rise for approximately 1 hour, or until doubled in size.

While the dough rises, prepare the vanilla custard. Split the vanilla pod lengthwise and scrape out the seeds. Add the seeds and pod to the remaining cup of milk in a saucepan and heat gently until steaming.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the 3 egg yolks, remaining 1/4 cup of granulated sugar and 2 tablespoons of cornstarch until smooth.
Remove the vanilla pod from the warm milk. Gradually pour the milk into the egg yolk mixture while whisking continuously to prevent the eggs from scrambling.

Return the custard mixture to the saucepan and cook over medium-low heat, whisking continuously until thickened and gently bubbling. Continue whisking for 1 minute, then transfer to a bowl, cover the surface and refrigerate until cooled.
Preheat the oven to 200°C (390°F). Gently press a deep indentation into the centre of each risen bun without deflating the surrounding dough.
Divide the cooled vanilla custard evenly between the six buns, spooning it into each indentation.
Bake for approximately 15–20 minutes, or until the buns are golden brown and the dough is fully baked. Transfer to a wire rack and allow to cool completely.
Prepare the glaze by mixing 1 cup of powdered sugar with 1–2 tablespoons of water, adding the water gradually until a thick, spreadable glaze forms.
Spread the glaze around the custard centre of each cooled bun and sprinkle generously with shredded coconut. Serve once the glaze has set. Refrigerate any leftovers within 2 hours.

recipes.name: Tom yum (hot & sour) soup with prawns

instructions.instruction_content: Prepare the aromatics. Lightly crush the lemongrass stalk and cut it into large pieces. Slice the galangal, tear the makrut lime leaves and lightly crush the green chillies. Separate the coriander leaves from the stems and roots.
Bring the 700ml of chicken stock to a boil in a medium saucepan. Add the lemongrass, galangal, coriander stems and roots if available, and makrut lime leaves.
Reduce the heat and simmer gently for 5 minutes to allow the aromatics to infuse the broth.

Add the peeled and deveined king prawns and green chillies. Simmer gently for 2–4 minutes, depending on their size, until the prawns are opaque and fully cooked to an internal temperature of 63°C (145°F).
Remove the saucepan from the heat. Add 1 tablespoon of fish sauce and the lime juice. Taste and gradually add more fish sauce if needed to achieve a balanced hot, sour and savory broth.

Remove the lemongrass, galangal, coriander stems and roots, makrut lime leaves and whole chillies. Divide the soup and prawns between two bowls, garnish with the reserved coriander leaves and serve hot.
Roughly chop the onion and tomato, slice the galangal and red chilli, and lightly crush the lemongrass stalks. Tear the makrut lime leaves and clean and slice the oyster mushrooms.
Pour 1.3 litres of water into a large saucepan and bring to a boil. Add the chicken stock cube and stir until dissolved.
Add the onion, tomato, red chilli, galangal, lemongrass and makrut lime leaves. Reduce the heat to medium and simmer for 20 minutes to allow the flavors to develop.
Remove the lemongrass, galangal and makrut lime leaves from the broth, leaving the onion, tomato and chilli in the saucepan.
Add the oyster mushrooms and simmer for 3–5 minutes until tender.
Stir in 1 tablespoon of sugar, 25ml of fish sauce, 70ml of coconut milk and 1 tablespoon of Thai chilli jam. Bring the soup to a gentle simmer.
Add the peeled and deveined raw king prawns. Simmer gently for 2–4 minutes, depending on their size, until the prawns are opaque and fully cooked to an internal temperature of 63°C (145°F).
Remove the saucepan from the heat and stir in 25ml of lime juice. Taste the broth and adjust the seasoning if needed. Divide between two serving bowls, garnish with fresh coriander and serve hot.

measurements.measure_value: 50ml for dipping sauce, plus extra for soaking

instructions.instruction_content: Prepare the dipping sauce by combining the juice of half a lime, 2 tablespoons of rice vinegar, 1 tablespoon of palm sugar, 3 tablespoons of fish sauce, the chopped birds-eye chilli and 50ml of water in a small bowl. Stir until the sugar dissolves and set aside.
Wash the carrot and courgette, then spiralize them or cut them into thin matchsticks. Trim any excessively long vegetable strands to make the rolls easier to assemble.
Wash and dry the mint and coriander leaves. Ensure the king prawns are fully cooked, peeled and deveined. Keep the prawns refrigerated until ready to assemble.
Fill a wide bowl with warm water and place a clean, damp tea towel on your work surface. Dip one rice paper sheet into the water according to the package instructions, then place it on the tea towel.
Place a few mint and coriander leaves in the centre of the rice paper sheet. Add two cooked king prawns and a small handful of the prepared carrot and courgette.
Fold the bottom edge of the rice paper over the filling, fold both sides inward, then roll tightly to enclose the filling completely. Be careful not to tear the wrapper.
Repeat with the remaining rice paper sheets and filling until you have six rolls.

Slice the rolls diagonally if desired and serve with the dipping sauce. If not serving immediately, cover and refrigerate. Consume within 24 hours and do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.

Place the chicken breast in a small saucepan and cover with water. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 12–18 minutes, depending on its thickness, until the internal temperature reaches 74°C (165°F).
Remove the chicken from the water and allow it to cool briefly. Slice into thin strips and refrigerate until ready to assemble the parcels.
Wash the vegetables and herbs. Cut the carrot and cucumber into thin matchsticks, thinly slice the red pepper, and separate the lettuce, mint and coriander leaves.
Prepare the rice noodles according to the package instructions. Drain well, rinse with cold water and cut into shorter strands to make assembly easier.
Prepare the rice flour pancakes according to the package instructions. Place each softened pancake on a clean, damp work surface.
Place a small portion of rice noodles, cooked chicken, carrot, cucumber, red pepper, mint and coriander about one-third of the way up the pancake, leaving enough space around the edges for folding.
Fold the bottom edge of the pancake over the filling, fold both sides inward and roll tightly to enclose the filling. Repeat with the remaining pancakes and filling.
Prepare the dipping sauce by mixing 2 tablespoons of fish sauce, 2 tablespoons of rice vinegar, the juice of half a lime and the sliced red chilli in a small bowl.

Arrange the parcels on a serving plate with the lettuce and remaining mint and coriander leaves. Wrap each parcel in a lettuce leaf with fresh herbs and enjoy with the dipping sauce. If not serving immediately, cover and refrigerate. Consume within 24 hours and do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.

measurements.measure_value: 2 tbsp, for sealing and dipping sauce

instructions.instruction_content: Mince the garlic, grate the ginger and carrot, and finely chop the celery and spring onions. Squeeze any excess moisture from the grated carrot.
Combine the ground pork, garlic, ginger, carrot, celery, spring onions, 1 tablespoon of soy sauce and 1 teaspoon of sesame seed oil in a bowl. Mix until evenly combined.
Separate the wonton wrappers and keep the unused wrappers covered with a slightly damp paper towel to prevent them from drying out.
Place a heaping teaspoon of pork filling in the center of each wonton wrapper. Avoid overfilling.
Lightly brush two adjacent edges of the wrapper with water. Fold the wrapper diagonally to form a triangle, pressing firmly around the filling to remove trapped air and seal the edges.
Bring the two outer corners of the triangle together, lightly moisten one corner with water and pinch them together to seal. Repeat with the remaining wrappers and filling.
Heat the vegetable oil in a deep, heavy-bottomed pot to 175°C (350°F). Do not fill the pot more than halfway with oil. Use a cooking thermometer to monitor the temperature.

Carefully lower 4–5 wontons into the hot oil using a slotted spoon. Fry for approximately 4–6 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden and the pork filling reaches an internal temperature of 71°C (160°F).
Remove the cooked wontons with a slotted spoon and drain on a wire rack or paper towels. Allow the oil to return to 175°C before frying the next batch. Repeat until all the wontons are cooked.
Prepare the dipping sauce in a clean bowl by combining the remaining 2 tablespoons of soy sauce, 1 teaspoon of sesame seed oil and 1 tablespoon of water.
Serve the wontons warm with the dipping sauce on the side. Refrigerate any leftovers within 2 hours and consume within 3 days.
